about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Mar rallied into the close to ~82.9, clearing Tuesday's highs and the 82.7 resistance as a weaker dollar and firmer crude helped outside money back in. No new supply or demand data; old-crop Mar/May keeps leaning on Texas Plains losses, but high-grade certs stay a two-sided risk for longs.
events: Dollar index slips, firmer crude (WSJ, Pro Farmer)

sugar.fundamental: London whites added about 1% in the only open sugar market, and the real firmed again to ~5.74 per dollar, extending the squeeze on centre-south mills' forward selling. Nothing new from Brazil on cane crush or the sugar/ethanol mix, so the Brazil-first picture is unchanged; Mar (last ~18.34) should open Friday with a firmer tone.
events: London white sugar ~522 (+1%) on Thanksgiving (ICE Europe)
Raw sugar near one-month high before the holiday (Reuters)

coffee.fundamental: Robusta bounced about 2% in London off its three-year low, though Vietnamese farm-gate prices are still slipping as the harvest moves, so the bounce looks like short-covering rather than tighter supply. The stronger real (~5.74) slows Brazilian selling; nothing new on ICE certified stocks or Brazil deliverability, which remain the anchor for Mar (~270).
events: London robusta ~2,863 (+2.3%) off a three-year low (Reuters, ICE Europe)
Vietnam coffee prices slide on harvest pressure (Reuters)

cocoa.fundamental: London cocoa is flat near 4,040 in thin trade with New York shut. No new Ivory Coast arrivals tally, no COCOBOD news and still no November ICCO quarterly bulletin, so slow arrivals versus rising ICE certified stocks keeps the market balanced.
events: Cocoa near one-month high into the holiday on slow Ivorian arrivals (Reuters, Barchart)
No November ICCO bulletin published yet (ICCO)
